title: Access and refresh tokens travel in URLs: the launcher, CMS 'Login', Content cards and the sales redirect all put them in ?token=&refreshToken=
evidence: code read; sos-bar dist ScopeItem.js:35 builds <app>/<locale>/auth?token=
repro: Open any app from the rail; the address bar and history hold the bearer token
status: partly fixed (053c1c8): Files and the Website Manager open with a one-time code, no token in any address; Tasks, HR, Sales, Marketing and Chats move in their waves; client CMS sites keep their own /auth contract

title: The /auth hand-off keeps the token in the URL (router.push, not replace) and follows ?redirect= unchecked: an open redirect
repro: Open /auth?token=<valid>&redirect=https://example.com: after 1 s the browser leaves for example.com; Back reopens the token URL

title: Impersonation stores the admin's whole original session (refresh token included) as plain JSON in sessionStorage, before the login-as call has even succeeded
repro: Log in as someone: sessionStorage holds the admin's tokens readable by any script

title: Exit impersonation is a dead end in any other tab: the saved session is per tab, so the banner sends you to login, and middleware sends a signed-in person back home
repro: Log in as Aya; open SOS in a new tab; press Exit: you land on / still as Aya, with no way back to your own account

title: Session cookies are readable by scripts (httpOnly false) for 7 days; SSO sessions without a refresh token are stored with an empty one, so the first 401 signs the person out
status: open: contract for the dev team (httpOnly session cookies, refresh tokens for SSO sessions)

title: The CMS account form is built around the API returning the account's password: it pre-fills the field, so saving an edit without touching it sends the mask (or the real password) back
repro: Edit an account, change only its name, save: the request carries the password field
status: fixed in the frontend (58225ad; verified 2026-10-01); contract: the API should never return the password
